items.name: steamed white rice
assumptions: Bowl re-assessed after challenge as a medium rice bowl with ~330 ml level interior capacity (~13-14 cm rim, thick walls, footed base), judged against the chopsticks (~23 cm) for scale
Heaped dome above the rim adds ~70 ml, giving ~400 ml in the bowl; cooked rice density ~0.8 g/ml → ~320 g
Spoon-held clump now counted as additional ~25-30 g because no scoop crater is visible in the bowl's surface (correction from challenge 3)

Energy density raised from 130 to 140 kcal/100g: grains are short/medium-grain and sticky (Japanese-style), which cooks drier than long-grain, but the rice looks moist/glossy so the full 160-168 kcal/100g Japanese-table value was not used
Plain steamed white rice, no added oil, butter, or seasoning visible
energy density from food database ('white rice, cooked')

scale_reference: medium Asian rice bowl (~330 ml level interior, ~13-14 cm rim) with chopsticks for scale
notes: Single-food photo; only plain steamed rice is visible. Remaining uncertainty is interior bowl volume (thick dark walls hide how much of the outer size is ceramic) and the exact water ratio used, which swings kcal/100g between roughly 130 and 165.

items.name: steamed white rice
assumptions: Bowl re-judged as a deep, steep-sided rice bowl, ~14 cm rim diameter, ~350 ml capacity (raised from 13 cm/300 ml after ruling that perspective magnifies the raised spoon in the frame)
Rice fills the bowl to the rim plus a ~60-70 ml dome above it, ~375 ml total in the bowl
Cooked rice density ~0.8 g/ml → ~300 g in the bowl
Lifted spoonful (~20 g) is now ADDED rather than netted out, because the rice surface in the bowl shows no scoop void (accepted challenge)
Plain steamed white rice, no butter, oil or seasoning (~130 kcal/100 g)
energy density from food database ('white rice, cooked')

scale_reference: deep Asian rice bowl (~14 cm rim, ~350 ml) and the metal spoon head (~4 cm wide), with allowance for the spoon being nearer the camera
notes: Only rice is visible; chopsticks and spoon are utensils, not food. Steam indicates freshly cooked plain rice with no visible fat or seasoning. Remaining uncertainty is bowl diameter and depth, worth roughly ±50 g; the spoonful is counted in addition to the bowl since no scoop cavity is visible.

items.name: red wine grapes (main cluster on the vine)
assumptions: Berry count revised upward after re-count of the packed front face (~75-80 visible across ~10 wide by 8-9 rows) plus a slightly smaller hidden back face, per accepted challenge
Wine-type grapes smaller than table grapes, ~2.6 g edible weight each
Energy density raised from 69 to 80 kcal/100 g for near-harvest, fully colored wine grapes at high Brix, discounted for thick skins and seeds
Stems excluded from edible weight
Fruit growing on a vine, not a plated serving

items.name: red wine grapes (second partial cluster, top right)

Only the unobstructed berries counted; the portion cut off by the frame edge and hidden behind the leaf is not included
Same berry size and energy density as the main cluster
